verses.text: When Rehoboam's kingdom was firmly set up and he was strong, he turned away from the LORD's law, and all Israel did the same.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam's rule, Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem, because the people had been unfaithful to the LORD.
He came with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen. With him came more soldiers from Egypt than anyone could count: Libyans, Sukkites, and Ethiopians.
He captured the walled towns of Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.

Then the prophet Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah, who had gathered in Jerusalem because of Shishak. He said to them, "The LORD says, 'You have left me, so now I have left you in Shishak's hands.'"
Then the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is right."

When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, his message came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves, so I will not destroy them. I will soon rescue them, and I will not pour out my anger on Jerusalem through Shishak.
But they will become his servants, so they can learn the difference between serving me and serving the kings of other countries."
So Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem. He took away the treasures of the LORD's temple and the treasures of the king's palace. He took everything, including the gold shields Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them and gave them to the commanders of the guards who kept watch at the palace door.
Whenever the king went into the LORD's temple, the guards came and carried the shields, and then took them back to the guardroom.
Because Rehoboam humbled himself, the LORD's anger turned away from him, and he was not completely destroyed. There were also some good things in Judah.

So King Rehoboam made himself strong in Jerusalem and ruled as king. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled for seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel as the place for his name. His mother was Naamah, from Ammon.
He did evil, because he did not set his heart on seeking the LORD.
Everything Rehoboam did, from beginning to end, is written in the records of the prophet Shemaiah and of Iddo the seer, in the family records. Rehoboam and Jeroboam were always at war.
Rehoboam died and was buried in the City of David. His son Abijah became king after him.
